title: Joint verification
summary: The verifier MUST own evidence correctness, the same cumulative evidence packet, and independent grading of the final fast result. The harness executes profiles. Product source stays read-only. Runtime structure MUST be repaired without changing actual signal; genuine proof and product failures remain blockers.
instructions: Verification MUST keep product source read-only. The verifier and harness MAY repair runtime evidence structure. They MUST preserve raw provenance, actual observations, assertions, criterion coverage, and recorded failures.

Verification evidence comes from the stage's declared parallel evidence workers: one review worker, and one QA worker when QA runs. The supervisor launches them top-level and in parallel, so each runs on its mapped model. The verifier consolidates their reports and MUST NOT launch subagents of its own. On a scoped return visit the invocation declares, no evidence worker runs: the verifier records each dimension the card assigns as its own section of `data.verify.dimensions`. Product source remediation remains outside verification.

The verifier MUST consume the incoming evidence packet reference supplied by its invocation and extend the same cumulative packet at data.verify.evidence_packet. It MUST retain prior observations, results, failures, waivers, repair records, and provenance while adding the current review and QA reconciliation, claim spot checks, criterion coverage, and final fast result. A stage return, invocation rename, or path change MUST NOT create a replacement bundle or erase earlier signal.

QA MUST run only when an acceptance criterion has proof `live`, when the change touches a user-facing surface, or when no criterion proof can be read. A user-facing surface is a plan file or implementation changed file with a `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.vue`, `.svelte`, `.html`, `.css`, or `.scss` extension. Otherwise verification is the reviewer plus the verifier. The verifier MUST then grade each `test` criterion from the test the implementation's acceptance evidence or `tests_added` names for it, plus the gate evidence that the test passed. A `test` criterion with no named test MUST fail. The harness decides from the run's plan output or specification and from the paths the plan and implementation outputs declare. It records a QA worker it did not launch on the invocation, and the card states the reason. That visit owes no `data.verify.qa_cases`.

An `observe` criterion needs a signal after ship, so it MUST NOT block verification. The verifier MUST record its result as `observe`. The harness refuses an `observe` result for a criterion whose declared proof is another type. It also refuses any other result for an `observe` criterion.

When evidence workers ran, the verifier MUST read every evidence report the card lists in full, and MUST cite each one in the cumulative packet and its consolidation. It MUST independently grade the harness-collected raw observations for pivotal claims and disputed reproductions rather than rerun a dimension wholesale. Missing observations MUST be requested by declared operation id in data.verification_execution_requests, with a non-empty reason and no executable definition. An undefined operation MUST use the existing blocked verification route and name missing_evidence_paths until a source-authorized stage supplies authority.

Except on a declared scoped return visit, a genuinely missing or empty evidence report is a blocked stage. Before declaring proof missing, the verifier and harness MUST resolve repairable runtime paths, aliases, and shapes when the actual report exists. A structural defect MUST NOT make existing equivalent evidence absent. The verifier MUST report blocked with the unresolved missing proof and MUST NOT substitute its own single-track pass for the absent dimension. A worker the card lists as not launched owes no report.
QA MUST NOT treat the implementer's self-evaluation as proof. Each QA case MUST record steps, expected result, actual result, and reproducible evidence.

Read-only evidence workers and the verifier MUST NOT execute shell commands or repository-check profiles. The harness MUST collect authorized bounded operations before QA and final verifier delegation and MUST run profiles and final policy-bound validators itself. Workers MUST cite current gate evidence for profile results and independently grade raw execution observations against expected behavior. Profile results MUST NOT substitute for live cases. QA MUST request additional observations through its report's .execution-request.json sidecar using only operation ids and reasons.

The harness MUST run the final configured fast profile after evidence correctness and the other required verify checks pass, and MUST append its actual result to the same cumulative evidence packet. The verifier independently grades the recorded result. The final verification gate MUST be fast, not full or a release profile. Ship and release commands MUST NOT run tests or validation checks. Interior gates use fast and static profiles.

After a remediation routes back to verify, the harness MUST recollect affected authorized observations against the current source fingerprint before read-only delegation. Unchanged requests within one invocation MUST reuse current observations without a launch loop. Superseded observations and consumer reports MUST remain historical evidence. The verifier MUST extend the same packet with refreshed affected proof and retain prior gate evidence only for checks the remediation cannot affect.

A verification that returns after a remediation MUST independently grade current harness-collected observations for QA cases that touch the remediation's blast radius. It MUST carry every other case forward with its earlier result. A carried case MUST record `carried_from` with the prior invocation id and the workspace fingerprint the result was observed at. This caps case coverage only and changes no profile allowance.

On a return visit after a remediation, the reviewer MUST review the remediation diff and the prior findings. It MUST confirm each prior finding as fixed or still open. A new finding in code the remediation did not change MUST block only at `blocker` severity. A lower new finding in that code is a warning, and the `pass_with_warnings` route sends it to the operator inbox. On a scoped return visit the verifier MUST apply the same rule to the review dimension.
Each finding MUST state its source (review or qa, which on a scoped return visit names the dimension that raised it), a severity, a statement, and reproducible evidence.
The joint verdict MUST be pass, pass_with_warnings, fail_remedial, or fail_severe, and the stage result MUST be success only for the two passing verdicts.

The verdict MUST be pass_with_warnings when three things hold. Every QA case that ran passes. Every acceptance criterion passes or records `observe`. Every finding is below blocker severity. The harness routes the demoted findings to the operator inbox, and the run advances without a remediation loop.
A non-blocking finding routed to the warning inbox SHOULD name the condition that makes it urgent. That condition stays separate from the chunk or owner that will close it, when the two differ.

Severity blocker is reserved for defects that make the change unsafe to ship or that impugn the verification itself: missing real proof, actual failures, unresolved contradictions, altered, weakened, deleted, or gamed assertions, acceptance criteria not actually covered, and security or data-loss concerns. A QA pass MUST NOT demote a blocker. Runtime normalization MUST NOT erase or recast these signals.
fail_severe is reserved for a fundamental failure of the approach, the plan, or the acceptance criteria, and the verifier MUST justify it in severity_rationale. Every other failure is fail_remedial.
A failing verdict MUST carry remediation_guidance stating the failing observation, the reproduction, and the expected behavior, actionable without access to the verifier.

The verifier owns incoming evidence correctness and runtime artifact diagnostics. The verifier and harness MUST normalize or repair formatting, shape, path, citation, timestamp, and identity defects when actual signal is unchanged. They MUST preserve raw provenance and record each repair, its original reference, and its corrected representation in the same cumulative packet. A structural defect alone MUST NOT block acceptance or route work to product remediation. These repairs MUST stay within runtime evidence and MUST NOT edit product source, invent proof, alter assertions, or hide failures.

A repository check that ultimately passes MUST NOT fail because of elapsed clock time. Slow successful checks are operator FYIs. Actual timeouts, hangs, nonzero exits, or failing assertions remain defects.

When the stage reports a failing or blocked verdict, the harness MUST route that verdict without running a repository-check profile. It MUST record each shell gate as skipped with the deciding reason. A failing verdict routes to remediate.

Before submission, the harness MUST apply the resolved policy-bound validators under VALID-001 to verify data, verdict consistency, QA cases, criterion coverage, execution currency, and the verification artifact. The verifier grades independently with file tools. Runtime repairs MUST retain raw provenance and repair records in data.verify.evidence_packet. Missing, failed, stale, wrong-identity, escaped, unauthorized, or profile-substituted observations MUST NOT permit passing required evidence. Command stdout alone MUST NOT establish a browser verdict.

Only the harness declares a scoped return visit, from the stage's `scoped_return` limits and the run record. The verifier MUST NOT declare one itself. These cost rules keep the evidence workers for a first visit, a fail_severe return, or a changed path under an excluded glob. A deleted test or a repair above the path or finding limit also keeps them. A test deletion committed inside the remediation escapes the deleted-path check. As a result, a deleted or weakened test in the blast radius stays a blocker, as the severity rule above states.
